notes:
- Your agent can now do a job on a website end to end: sign in where you sign in, click through,
  download what it came for, hand it to you, and keep it. Most of this release is that one job,
  found by collecting a real bank statement over and over until there was nothing left to go wrong.
- The browser window opens on your Mac's own chip. It was launching the Intel build through Rosetta,
  which is the whole reason the window it opened felt slow.
- The Websites panel says whether each site is signed in, and when it last was. It said nothing, so
  a site that had signed you out looked exactly like one that had not.
- Closing the sign-in window is noticed. The panel used to keep saying the window was open, because
  it watched for the program rather than for a page, and closing the last window does not close
  Chrome.
- "A window just opened" is now said when a window has opened, rather than when the program was
  still starting.
- Your agent stops reloading over your sign-in. Asked to open a site it was already looking at, it
  went back to the front page, which on a bank signs you straight back out.
- A file a site hands over lands where the job can find it, and the job waits for it to arrive. It
  was being told where to put downloads one tab at a time, so four or five statements went to a
  folder nobody looked in, and a file still arriving when the browser closed was reported as one
  that never started.
- The same file handed over twice arrives once.
- "I'll do this bit" ends with a button. You had to type "done" at an agent that had just given you
  buttons for everything else.
- Your agent can read back the question it asked you. It sends a question as the caption on a
  picture of the screen, and could not see that caption afterwards, so your answer meant nothing to
  it and the job went round in circles.
- It stops handing you the clicking. Asked to sign in, it now names the window already open in front
  of you, instead of a screen inside Archie that does not exist.
- A browser job gets the room to finish. Every job stopped after ten steps, and for a browser a step
  is a click: one bank statement spent all ten opening the site, clicking through, downloading the
  PDF, sending it to its owner and filing the record, and then said "Reached the tool call limit"
  underneath the statement it had just collected.
- A job that does run out of steps now says what it finished and what is left, rather than reporting
  the whole thing as lost.
- The "let this agent use websites" warning has a button that takes you to the switch.
- Pictures and files arrive in the Archie window, not only on your phone. A statement your agent had
  just written to a folder six inches away showed up in the window as a sentence telling you it had
  gone to Telegram.
- Your agent can read a file it downloaded for you. It fetched a bank statement, sent it over, and
  twenty minutes later said it could not see the Downloads folder and asked for the file to be
  uploaded.
- A PDF whose text cannot be read says so instead of guessing at it. Some PDFs come apart into
  nonsense that still looks like words: in a real bank statement every date and amount arrived
  scrambled, and the agent decoded most of them and got four wrong, including ten dollars going out
  that became a hundred and ten dollars coming in. Those lines are now taken out and named as
  missing.
- A total in a spreadsheet your agent writes is the sum of the rows it wrote, never a figure copied
  in from somewhere else.
- Your agent can change one number in a spreadsheet you already have. "Add this to my expenses"
  used to end in a second spreadsheet and an evening merging the two.
- A spreadsheet it reads says what it cannot see. Colors, merged banners and frozen rows are how a
  real sheet tells three tables apart, and it was answering as though the numbers were the whole
  truth.
- Statement Collector collects each account on the day that account's statement is ready, instead of
  doing the whole round on one date. A card closing on the 3rd and one closing on the 27th are three
  weeks apart, and neither is late. It works the dates out from the mail that already arrives, so
  there is no list to keep.
- It asks once what you want done with a statement, with buttons: a running spreadsheet, a summary
  of what changed, or both. Then it remembers and never asks again.
- Asking your agent to forget something now forgets it. It had a button for this on one screen and
  was told in as many words that it had no way to do it, so "forget that I play Rocket League" got
  directions to a screen instead. Anything it forgets can be put back.
- Your agent picks things up as you talk, without being asked to remember them, and a hobby it
  picked up can no longer push a deadline out of its memory.
- Something a correspondent said about their own life can no longer end up in your agent's memory
  of you.
- Two texts sent one after the other get one reply covering both. The card answering the first was
  retired half a minute later by a card that answered only the second, so the first answer was not
  wrong, it was gone.
- A reply drafted for you sounds like you, not like the person who wrote to you.
- An account on the Connections tab says whether the mailbox actually opens, not only what it was
  allowed to do. A withdrawn permission, a changed password and a revoked account all looked like
  eight green ticks on a mailbox that had not opened in a week.
- You can say which model each of the three response quality settings uses, if you are paying per
  token on your own key and already know which one you want.
- The spending page stopped telling people on DeepSeek and Mistral that they were spending nothing.
- Groq is described as the cheapest option rather than the free one. Its free tier cannot run a
  single Archie turn, and we were recommending it first.
- Fixed: a GPT-5 model left thinking spent its whole reply budget on thinking and answered nothing.
- Fixed: typing /new in the Archie window looked like it hung. The confirmation had already arrived
  and was sitting one line above the message asking for it.
- Fixed: a picture or a note sent while your agent was still writing appeared under the reply
  instead of above it, so you read the answer, then the button you had already tapped, then the
  question that button was answering.
- Asking your agent whether the store has something now searches the store. It answered from memory,
  or said it could not look.
- An add-on installed from chat says when it is ready. It said "ready in a few seconds" and then
  went quiet, because what makes it work is a restart.
- Fixed: saving as you type was restarting your agent as you type.
- Fixed: the Back arrow could not undo moving to a section of a page, only to another page.
- Fixed: an error screen threw away the half of the message that said what happened, and stayed
  after the problem was gone.
- Fixed: one long line in a routine could push a whole tab off the side of the window.
